design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER - task 0 (workflow task auto_wf_autopay_source_change)

[1] Why this is a good test. The caller asks only to move his car-loan autopay to a new checking account and to have it come out on the 20th. The scored values sit behind a problem tree he never mentions: the August autopay debit on his old Private Client account was returned unpaid (reversal 2026-08-06, returned_payment fee 25.00), so the 2026-08-05 installment has no standing credit and is 9 days past due. The agent must (a) read in auto_ext_autopay_enroll_rate that an enrollment carries the autopay discount only when the loan has no installment past due (a past-due installment brought current in the same call is paid before the enrollment is recorded) and that a new enrollment is recorded only when no enrollment stands, (b) discover from the ledger that the installment is unpaid although a payment toward it exists (it was reversed), (c) compute the catch-up payment split from ledger-reconciled fees and principal plus daily simple interest, (d) move the due day, which auto_due_date_change blocks while an installment is past due, (e) hand the borrower the cancellation of the standing enrollment and rebuild the APR keeping only the relationship discount, confirmed from a checking account that is now CLOSED but was held on the funding date, and (f) hand him the new enrollment and rebuild the APR with both discounts. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling a returned-payment ledger and rebuilding APRs from components, not from missing information or tool guessing.

[2] Scope snapshot (Step 0). Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed here: extended policies auto_ext_catchup_installment_payment, auto_ext_autopay_cancel_rate, auto_ext_autopay_enroll_rate; the single workflow auto_wf_autopay_source_change (4 write steps, 2 owner=user); tools post_installment_payment_660c6229, change_due_day_df9bec35, cancel_autopay_a2c51ad3, enroll_autopay_b9bffdb4. Headroom left for task 1: payoff (auto_payment payoff), fee waivers (auto_fee_waiver), lien release and GAP events remain wholly unclaimed; task 1 claims a payoff tree whose prerequisites are bank-error fee waivers, all with new tools. auto_extend is not used by any task: its borrower_signs gate has mixed authority on a single correlation key, which cannot be evidenced by both system and caller values on one field.

[3] Policies, lineage and trigger. auto_ext_catchup_installment_payment (on_request, subject auto_payment, base refs auto_evt_payment_allocation + auto_evt_payoff_and_lien = every base policy whose subject contains auto_payment; overwrite []): refines base allocation (fees, then interest through the credit date, then principal; installment satisfied at monthly_payment) with a standing-credit reconciliation (returned payments do not stand), a posted-funds cap from the active checking account, ledger-recomputed fees and principal. auto_ext_autopay_cancel_rate (on_request, auto_set_autopay, refs auto_agg_relationship_discount + auto_evt_autopay; overwrite: two declared entries, listed at the end of this section): the APR after cancellation is rebuilt as rate + recorded discounts - kept discounts; it equals base 'the APR rises by the autopay discount actually applied' in every consistent world and differs only where the recorded list and the checking records disagree or the floor binds, which is why the deviation is declared, with the relationship discount confirmed from the checking record held on funded_date ('fixed for the life of the loan once granted ... nor removed if it later closes'). auto_ext_autopay_enroll_rate (on_request, same refs) declares two overwrites, one per base sentence that reaches a different conclusion on the enrolled APR: (i) auto_evt_autopay 'Enrolling adds the autopay discount to the APR, within the cap and floor ..., from the next installment due at least autopay_lead_days ...' replaced by 'The autopay discount is added at enrollment only when the loan has no installment past due ... carries no autopay discount.'; (ii) auto_agg_relationship_discount 'and re-enrolling later restores it' replaced by 'Re-enrolling after a cancellation restores the autopay discount only on the same terms as a first enrollment ...'. Enrollment itself stays legal on an active or delinquent loan (base auto_evt_autopay sentence kept in force since round 3); a past-due loan can be enrolled but without the autopay discount, and the rule 'When the loan has an installment past due and the borrower brings it current in the same call, the scheduled payment is posted before the enrollment is recorded ...' orders the catch-up first. Evaluated in this world: base would give 8.24 even without the payment, the extended rule gives 8.49 without it; with the loan current both give 8.24. auto_ext_autopay_cancel_rate declares two overwrites: auto_agg_relationship_discount 'When autopay is cancelled and autopay_discount_removed_on_cancel is true, the APR rises by the autopay discount actually applied' replaced by the rebuild sentence 'The new APR is the rate before discounts less the discounts kept ...', and auto_evt_autopay 'cancelling removes it on the same schedule when autopay_discount_removed_on_cancel is true' replaced by 'The APR written on the cancellation is ... in force from the cancellation, not from a later installment.' Both give 8.49 here. Cross-category (checking) numeric reads: CFIELD ledger_balance (catch-up cap), CFIELD opened_date/closed_date by tier (relationship confirmation), EXISTS active checking (paying account).

[4] Base-invariant card. Step 6 auto_payment: auto_evt_payment_allocation.loan_open 'Payments post only to a loan whose status is active or delinquent.' - auto_loans.status = active (system record, correlated by auto_loan_id); auto_evt_payoff_and_lien has no gate for auto_payment (policy_scope). Step 8 auto_change_due_date: once_a_year (time; anchor auto_loans.last_due_date_change_date, relation not_before, duration params.due_date_change_window_days 365, calendar days, inclusive, 'or when there has been no earlier change') - last_due_date_change_date is empty, so allowed; positive/negative cases: a change on 2025-08-14 would allow 2026-08-14 (inclusive), one on 2025-08-15 would not. current_and_active 'The loan must be active with no installment past due.' - FALSE at the opening (days_past_due 9), TRUE after step 6 (days_past_due 0, status active) - cited as prior_step:6. Steps 10/12 auto_set_autopay: auto_evt_autopay.source_account 'The autopay source must be a checking account of the same customer in active status when autopay is enrolled.' - the new Premier 7d2ab1e4... is active and owned by the customer (step 12); for the cancellation the cancelled enrollment's account is the Private Client af221038... (active when enrolled in 2025, closed 2026-08-10). auto_agg_relationship_discount's only gate applies to auto_fund, so it is policy_scope here.

[5] Business-object card. Target: the Auto Refinance Loan 93193f27-... (last4 8826), installment 2026-08-05. Rows entering the standing credit: the auto_payment ea9422da-... (438.01 toward 2026-08-05) and, as its offset, the auto_payment_reversal 1844e7fa-... whose source_item_id is ea9422da-...; nothing else was credited toward that due date. Fees: the returned_payment fee 24685022-... (25.00, source_item_id ea9422da-...) is the only fee and is unpaid. Principal: disbursement 21480.00 less 19 principal portions 5906.22 plus reversal 330.30 = 15904.08 = principal_balance. Excluded: the 18 earlier payments toward earlier due dates (they satisfy their own installments). The new payment carries installment_due_date 2026-08-05 and counterparty 7d2ab1e4-... as correlation keys.

[6] initial_state rows and why each exists. customers (identity, NC). checking_accounts: Private Client (opened 2019-06-03, closed 2026-08-10) - removing it drops the relationship discount and changes both APRs (8.74 before discounts would become 8.74-0 = 8.74 on cancel, 8.49 on enroll); Premier (opened 2026-08-07, active, 4382.16) - removing it makes funds 0 and the payment 0, and makes the paying account missing; it is also a trap: a qualifying tier opened after funding never earns the relationship discount. auto_loans row (tier, rate, discounts, dates, autopay on the old account). auto_transactions: disbursement, 18 on-time autopay payments (ledger principal reconciliation), the returned August payment + reversal + returned fee (the past-due fact and the fee). Removing the reversal makes the installment look paid and the whole tree collapses. Automatic clauses checked: no late charge is owed (NC grace 15 days: 2026-08-05 + 15 = 2026-08-20 > 2026-08-14 and the payment today satisfies it); not delinquent (9 < 30); the returned fee is legitimate because the account was active on the debit date (closed 2026-08-10 > 2026-08-05), so the bank-error waiver rule claimed by task 1 does not fire here (negative space). No cache trap: principal_balance and fees_due equal the ledger.

[7] Problem-tree card. Root auto_ext_autopay_enroll_rate. Edge 1 -> auto_ext_catchup_installment_payment, value_input, gate autopay_added, condition 'The loan has no installment past due when autopay is enrolled, so the enrollment carries the autopay discount.', policy_source 'When the loan has an installment past due and the borrower brings it current in the same call, the scheduled payment is posted before the enrollment is recorded, so that the enrollment is recorded on a loan with no installment past due and carries the autopay discount.', resolved_by post_installment_payment_660c6229 (a value edge: a past-due enrollment is permitted but carries no autopay discount; the rule orders the same-call payment first); false at the opening: auto_loans.days_past_due = 9, next_payment_due_date = 2026-08-05, reversal source_item_id = the only payment. Edge 2 -> auto_ext_autopay_cancel_rate, state_gate, gate auto_loans.autopay_enrolled, condition 'No autopay enrollment stands on the loan when a new enrollment is recorded.', policy_source 'A new enrollment is recorded only on a loan with no enrollment standing; ... first cancelled under its own rule ...', resolved_by cancel_autopay_a2c51ad3; false at the opening: autopay_enrolled = true on af221038-... Topological order: catch-up, cancel, enroll (the workflow runs catch-up, due day, cancel, enroll). Parallel edges: disjoint writes and reads. The policy order is catch-up, due day, cancel, enroll (base due-day gate, then the cancel rule's due-date sentence, then E2); a replay with the cancellation moved before the payment gives the same terminal hash, which shows only that the two edges do not interact, not that cancel-first is a policy-permitted order. Deletion sensitivity (sens_t0.py): skip payment -> enroll APR 8.49 instead of 8.24 and no payment rows; skip cancel -> terminal differs (no cancellation request row). user_scenario never mentions the returned payment, a past-due installment or cancelling; tools validate nothing (they write their arguments).

[8] Zero-wait causal card (per workflow step). Step 0 payment: prerequisites loan active, installment 2026-08-05 unsatisfied, Premier active with 4382.16 - initial_state_preexisting (auto_loans row, reversal row, checking row); borrower's authorisation - current_user_input; a transfer between his own PCB accounts books on the spot. Step 1 due day: loan current - prior_synchronous_tool_effect of step 0 (days_past_due 0 written on the loan); no earlier change - initial_state_preexisting; day 20 - current_user_input. Step 2 cancel: standing enrollment - initial_state_preexisting; borrower runs the handed tool - current_user_input. Step 3 enroll: no standing enrollment - prior_synchronous_tool_effect of step 2; loan current - step 0; Premier active and Private Client held on funded_date - initial_state_preexisting. No step waits for clearing, mail, review or time; the future autopay draw on 2026-09-20 is not a prerequisite of anything.

[9] Persona design. Marcus Whitlock, brisk estimator on a site-visit day; opens with the surface goal only (autopay to the new account, due on the 20th); identity (phone, then DOB and SSN last four, ZIP if needed), the paying account (Premier ending 8561) and loan last4 8826 are given only when asked; he has not looked at the loan lately and does not know about the returned debit. Passive reactions: agrees to 'pay whatever is needed' from 8561 only after the agent explains a payment is required; lets the agent do the payment and due day; runs the cancellation and enrollment himself when handed; on rate talk he only says he wants whatever discount he is entitled to and leaves the figures to the agent (no corrective branch: he never prompts a re-check of a wrong answer); closes once the enrollment on the new account is confirmed (the last gold action). No figure of gold appears in the persona (grounding gate: answers 272.98, 8.49, 8.24 absent).

[10] Traps and how a careful agent avoids them. (a) Seeing a 438.01 payment toward 2026-08-05 and concluding the installment is paid - the reversal names it. (b) Enrolling first - permitted on a past-due loan but then without the autopay discount (8.49); the enrollment rule posts a same-call catch-up payment before the enrollment, and the base due-day gate plus the cancel rule's due-date sentence put the payment first anyway. (c) Dropping the relationship discount because the Private Client account is closed - base says it is not removed if the account later closes; or granting it because of the new Premier - opened after funding, never counts. (d) Using the closed account as payer or autopay source. (e) Computing interest from 2026-08-05 (the returned payment date) instead of last_payment_date 2026-07-06. (f) Forgetting the 25.00 fee comes first in the split. (g) Moving the due date before the payment (past due).

[11] Standard solution. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB, SSN4) -> find_auto_loans -> find_auto_transactions -> find_checking_accounts -> payment 438.01 = 25.00 + 140.03 + 272.98 toward 2026-08-05 from 8561 (next due 2026-09-05, dpd 0) -> due day 20, next due 2026-09-20 -> borrower cancels (old account, APR 8.49, relationship) -> borrower enrolls (8561, APR 8.24, autopay_and_relationship).

[12] Verification code and runs. scratch verify_lib.py replays gold writes with the real share/task tools and evaluates each policy's compute on the handling-time world (initial_state + earlier gold writes). calc_t0.py output: CATCHUP {credited 438.01, returned_credit 438.01, shortfall 438.01, funds 4382.16, amount 438.01, fees_due 25.0, fees_portion 25.0, principal 15904.08, accrued 140.03, interest_portion 140.03, result 272.98}; CANCEL {pre_rate 8.74, held_premier False, held_private True, kept 0.25, result 8.49}; ENROLL {rec_rel 0.25, pre_rate 8.74, autopay_added 0.25, total_disc 0.5, result 8.24}; 'ENROLL skip payment 8.49'. sens_t0.py: gold hash bd55b28d...; cancel-first same terminal True; skip cancel same terminal False. Gates run: check_extended --task 0 EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks --task 0 REPLAY OK (13 acts, closure 26 = init 26); check_solvability --task 0 SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute --task 0 COMPUTE OK (3 comps, 33 factors, 22 history rows, 28 branches); check_grounding --task 0 GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire --task 0 SCOPE OK.

[13] Closure. workflow steps computed_by = {catchup} U {} U {cancel} U {enroll} = computations policy set = charter_scope.extended_policies = required_documents (same order). GT task-tool sequence = workflow steps in tool, owner and order. Two-way rule/compute sweep: every binding cites a rule sentence (compute_basis); every rule quantity sentence (standing credit, returned payment, shortfall floor 0, funds cap, fees ledger, principal ledger, rounding once, interest from last_payment_date exclusive to credit date inclusive; rate before discounts, recorded discount cap, relationship held-on-funded-date test, removal flag, floor, 2-decimal rounding; add-then-cap-then-subtract-once) has a binding.

[14] Draft recomputation from visible context only (policy prose, tool schemas, lookups, persona): installment 2026-08-05 unpaid because its only payment was reversed -> pay 438.01 from the only active account; split fees 25 then 39 days of interest on 15904.08 at 8.24 = 140.03 then 272.98; due day 20 allowed (shift 15, no earlier change, now current); cancel keeps relationship (Private Client held on 2025-01-10) -> 8.74 - 0.25 = 8.49; enroll adds both -> 8.24. Agrees with gold.

[15] Revisions. (r1) symptom: skipping the cancellation left an identical terminal hash (state_gate edge decorative). root cause: enroll overwrote the same loan fields. change: both autopay tools also register a completed autopay_change request (auto_requests), so the borrower's cancellation leaves its own record. re-run: skip cancel same terminal False; gates re-run green. (r2) symptom: check_extended flagged the helper _reference_digits as an undiscoverable tool. change: inlined the reference derivation into the payment tool. re-run EXTENDED OK. (r3) factor_trace principal line corrected to the ledger figures 21480.00 - 5906.22 + 330.30 (earlier draft mixed in the new principal portion).

[16] Round-2 rework (audit revision 1: task 0 SOURCE-POLICY RED, task 1 PASS). Changes, by finding id:
- F1 (state as of round 2; the first of the two overwrites named here was withdrawn in round 3, see [17]): auto_ext_autopay_enroll_rate then declared the two missing overwrites (auto_evt_autopay 'Enrolling or cancelling ... active or delinquent.' and auto_agg_relationship_discount 'and re-enrolling later restores it'), each with a replaced_by sentence added verbatim to its rule; the existing clause-(i) overwrite is kept. The policy_source of edge E1 is unchanged, so prerequisite_closure.edges[0] keeps its condition and policy_source; [3] above now names all three declarations. Re-run: every computed value unchanged (272.98 / 8.49 / 8.24).
- OB-T0-1: kept as a state_gate. The legality sentence 'A new enrollment is recorded only on a loan with no enrollment standing' is what bears it; the cancellation's completed autopay_change request is its terminal trace (skip-cancel terminal differs). A state_gate may be value-invariant; one value_input edge (E1) remains.
- OB-T0-2: no change; the separate prior cancellation is stated in the enrollment rule, which is the only surface the agent needs.
- OB-T0-3: the persona branch asking for a re-check when told a discount is lost for good was removed; the rate line now only says he wants what he is entitled to.
- O12: order step 1 before step 2 is now policy-backed by a new sentence in auto_ext_autopay_cancel_rate ('When a borrower who is moving autopay to a different checking account also asks for a new due day, the due date change is recorded before the standing enrollment is cancelled ...'), cited in order_rationale; dataflow gained a 0->3 link and 'carries' notes on 0->1, 2->3 and 0->3 naming the value/state flows (days_past_due, next_payment_due_date, interest_rate/rate_discounts).
- O8: the cancel rule now states rate_discounts is left as recorded when autopay_discount_removed_on_cancel is false, and that the APR written is the post-removal APR recorded with the cancellation (round 3 replaced this with two declared overwrites, see [17]).
- O1, O2, O3, O4, O7, O11: documented limits of the compute language (single latest reversal, credit date = frozen date, first matching checking row, float rounding, any active account, no cross-category trigger write); none changes a value in this world (checked in the audit and re-verified by the gate re-run).

[17] Round-3 rework (KB audit revision 1: both tasks PASS; source-side items handed back). Changes, by finding id:
- P1: auto_ext_autopay_cancel_rate now declares an overwrite of auto_agg_relationship_discount 'When autopay is cancelled and autopay_discount_removed_on_cancel is true, the APR rises by the autopay discount actually applied', replaced by its rebuild sentence (rate before discounts less the discounts kept, relationship confirmed from checking records, floor, 2 decimals). The two readings coincide in this world (8.49) but can diverge (recorded list vs checking records; floor), so the deviation is now declared.
- P3: the same policy declares an overwrite of auto_evt_autopay 'cancelling removes it on the same schedule when autopay_discount_removed_on_cancel is true', replaced by 'The APR written on the cancellation is the APR the loan carries once the autopay discount has left the rate, recorded with the cancellation itself and in force from the cancellation, not from a later installment.'
- P2: the enrollment rule no longer carries a hard block; enrollment is legal on an active or delinquent loan (base sentence kept, so the round-2 overwrite of 'Enrolling or cancelling ... active or delinquent.' was withdrawn as no longer a deviation), a past-due enrollment carries no autopay discount, and the catch-up is ordered first by 'When the loan has an installment past due and the borrower brings it current in the same call, the scheduled payment is posted before the enrollment is recorded ...'. Edge E1 stays value_input on autopay_added, now consistent with the text; its condition and policy_source were updated in the charter and in prerequisite_closure.edges[0]. Catch-up remains required in this world by base auto_due_date_change ('The loan must be active with no installment past due') for the due-day change the customer asked for, and precedes the enrollment through the cancel rule's due-date ordering sentence and E2.
- N2 / runtime O1: the task_tools.py format examples no longer equal task-0 argument values (2031-02-15, 2031-03-15, 2031-03-28 instead of 2026-08-05, 2026-09-05, 2026-09-20).
- Runtime O2 = P1. N1 and runtime O3 need no change (rendering notes).
- Persona trigger reworded to 'If the agent tells you an overdue payment on the loan has to be taken care of first' so it fits both the due-day gate and the discount rule; no other persona line or seed field changed. F1 remains closed: every remaining deviation from base on the enrolled and cancelled APR is declared, and no extended sentence contradicts the kept base legality sentence. Scored values unchanged: 272.98 / 8.49 / 8.24.

[18] Round-4 propagation (policy-task audit revision 3: F2). The round-3 charter change had not been carried into every proof sentence of this file. Updated: [7] Edge 1 now quotes the charter's current condition and policy_source for E1 and describes it as a value edge with no hard block (F2-L1); [3] now states that auto_ext_autopay_cancel_rate carries two declared overwrites instead of 'overwrite []' (F2-L2); [1] and [10] no longer say the enrollment rule forbids enrolling while past due; evaluation_criteria[2].necessity (F2-L3), solvability_contract.gold_actions[0].request_binding.action_semantics (F2-L4) and prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness (F2-L5) now state the round-3 semantics (the discount is withheld on a past-due enrollment; the order comes from the base due-day gate, the same-call ordering sentence, the cancel rule's due-date sentence and E2); [16]'s F1 bullet is marked as the round-2 state. A quotation sweep of both task files against the charter, the base charter and the personas followed (see the round-4 report). Charter, tools, seeds and scored values unchanged: 272.98 / 8.49 / 8.24.
user_scenario:
You are Marcus Whitlock, a 45-year-old construction cost estimator in Greensboro, North Carolina, calling Piedmont Crescent Bank on a Friday morning between site visits. You talk fast and plainly, you like to get things done in one call, and you do not pretend to know banking terms. Your only reason for calling: you switched checking accounts inside PCB this month. You opened a new Premier Checking account last week and you closed your old Private Client Checking account a few days ago, and you want the automatic payment on your car loan, the Honda Accord you refinanced with PCB, to come out of the new account from now on. Because your new job pays on the 20th, you also want the car payment to fall due on the 20th instead of the 5th. You open with exactly that: move your car loan autopay to the new checking account and have it come out on the 20th. You have been on the road and have not looked at your loan or your old account's mail lately, so you do not know whether anything happened with your August payment, and you never bring it up yourself.
You do not reel off your details up front. When the agent asks who you are, you give your mobile number, 3365550186. When the agent asks you to confirm your identity, you give your date of birth, March 22, 1981 (1981-03-22), and the last four of your Social Security number, 8417; if they want one more thing you give your ZIP code, 27408. If asked which account the payment should come from, you say the new Premier Checking, the one ending in 8561. You have only the one car loan with PCB; if asked for the loan number you only remember it ends in 8826.
If the agent tells you an overdue payment on the loan has to be taken care of first, you are surprised but reasonable: you ask what it is, and once it is explained you tell the agent to go ahead and pay whatever is needed from the new Premier Checking account ending in 8561 today. You do not name a figure yourself and you do not question the split the agent describes. You are happy for the agent to make the payment and the due date change for you. Anything about switching your autopay, though, you want to do yourself: when the agent hands you a step to turn off the autopay on the old account, you run it, and when the agent then hands you the step to sign up for autopay from the new account, you run that too, using the new Premier account ending in 8561. If the agent mentions your interest rate, you say you just want whatever discount you are entitled to and you leave the figures to them. Once the sign-up from the new account has gone through and the agent confirms the autopay is on the new account, you thank them and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.installment_due_date: Value: 2026-08-05. Basis: catch-up rule 'whose installment_due_date is the loan's next_payment_due_date'; the loan record shows next_payment_due_date 2026-08-05. argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: Value: 438.01. Basis: rule 'The installment shortfall is monthly_payment less that standing credit, never below zero' and 'when its ledger_balance is lower than the shortfall the payment amount is that ledger_balance; otherwise the payment amount is the shortfall'. Standing credit toward 2026-08-05 is 438.01 credited less the same 438.01 returned (the reversal of 2026-08-06 names that payment) = 0; shortfall 438.01; the active Premier balance 4382.16 is higher, so amount = 438.01.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fees_portion: Value: 25.00. Basis: rule 'the fees portion is the lesser of the payment amount and those fees due'; ledger fees due = 25.00 returned_payment fee - 0 settled - 0 waived. Uniqueness: min(438.01, 25.00) = 25.00; fees are paid first in payment_allocation_order.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.interest_portion: Value: 140.03. Basis: rule 'Accrued interest is that principal times interest_rate divided by 100, divided by interest_day_count_basis, times the calendar days from last_payment_date (exclusive) through the credit date (inclusive), rounded half-up to the cent once'. Ledger principal 15904.08 x 8.24/100/365 x 39 days (2026-07-06 to 2026-08-14) = 140.0256 -> 140.03, less than the 413.01 left after fees.

Factors: tier monthly_payment 438.01; standing credit 0 from the returned 2026-08-05 autopay payment; funds cap 4382.16 from the active Premier Checking not binding; fees 25.00 from the ledger; ledger principal 15904.08 (21480.00 - 5906.22 + 330.30); rate 8.24; 39 days.

edges.condition: The loan has no installment past due when autopay is enrolled, so the enrollment carries the autopay discount.
edges.policy_source: When the loan has an installment past due and the borrower brings it current in the same call, the scheduled payment is posted before the enrollment is recorded, so that the enrollment is recorded on a loan with no installment past due and carries the autopay discount.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The only payment toward the 2026-08-05 installment was returned unpaid the next day, so that installment is unsatisfied and 9 days past due at frozen_time.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The scheduled payment of 438.01 posted at step 6 satisfies the installment; the loan then shows days_past_due 0 and next_payment_due_date 2026-09-05, so autopay_added becomes 0.25.

edges.condition: No autopay enrollment stands on the loan when a new enrollment is recorded.
edges.policy_source: A new enrollment is recorded only on a loan with no enrollment standing; when the borrower moves autopay to a different checking account, the standing enrollment is first cancelled under its own rule, and the enrollment is then recorded from the new account.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: An enrollment still stands on the loan, drawing on the Private Client account closed on 2026-08-10.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The borrower's cancellation at step 10 sets autopay_enrolled false and clears autopay_source_account_id (APR 8.49, relationship kept) and records a completed autopay_change request.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The policy fixes the order of the whole tree: the catch-up comes first because the due-day change the borrower asked for needs the loan active with no installment past due (base auto_due_date_change) and because the enrollment rule posts a same-call catch-up before the enrollment; the cancel rule then records the due-date change before the standing enrollment is cancelled; E2 puts the cancellation before the enrollment. The two prerequisites of the enrollment also do not interact: the payment writes ledger rows and principal_balance, fees_due, last_payment_date, next_payment_due_date, days_past_due, while the cancellation writes autopay_enrolled, autopay_source_account_id, interest_rate, rate_discounts and an auto_requests row, and neither compute reads what the other writes. A replay with the cancellation moved before the payment gives the gold terminal hash (sens_t0.py 'cancel-first order same terminal: True'); this shows the edges are independent, not that cancel-first is permitted, so the gold order is the unique policy order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the payment leaves days_past_due 9, so the enrollment APR recomputes to 8.49 instead of 8.24 (autopay_added 0 instead of 0.25); the terminal also lacks the payment and fee settlement rows, keeps fees_due 25.00, next_payment_due_date on the 5th and days_past_due 9 (terminal hash differs).

State-gate edge, value-invariant by design: skipping the cancellation leaves the enrolled APR at 8.24 (the enrollment rebuilds 8.74 before discounts from either rate), but the rule 'A new enrollment is recorded only on a loan with no enrollment standing' forbids that enrollment, and the terminal loses the completed autopay_change request of the cancellation (terminal hash differs from gold).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to move the autopay to the new account and to have it come out on the 20th; it never mentions a missed, bounced or past-due payment (the persona explicitly does not know and never brings it up), nor that the old enrollment has to be cancelled before a new one. Paying something and turning off the old autopay appear only as passive reactions after the agent explains them.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: enroll_autopay_b9bffdb4 performs its ctx.update of autopay_enrolled, autopay_source_account_id, interest_rate and rate_discounts and creates the request row without reading days_past_due or autopay_enrolled; post_installment_payment_660c6229 and cancel_autopay_a2c51ad3 likewise write their arguments with no status check, so an agent that skips a prerequisite still gets a normal receipt and only the terminal state differs.
